materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo of a thin silver laptop lying half open on beige floor tiles at the bottom of a carpeted staircase, photographed from in front of the lid so that the lid fills the frame and only the silver front edge of the base shows. The switched-off black screen has a long crack running diagonally across it, and the lid hangs loose at an odd angle at the left corner because the hinge there has snapped. The silver lid edges are plain. Morning daylight. No people, no text, no logos.

design.notes: Plan feature none with condition missing_information. The receipt leaves out the item description (and so the serial number), a required field of a receipt; it still shows the seller, the purchase date, the amount and the payment method.

triage.rationale: Accidental damage to one laptop (NZD 1,899) at the insured address, nobody hurt, photo supplied, policy on file. The only proof of purchase does not say what was bought, so ownership of this laptop is not shown and the serial label photo can only come later; required material is incomplete. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Purchase date 27 April 2026 is before the incident on 15 September 2026

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (10 February 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2020-02-10, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
